title: SYSK Selects: What Is a Shotgun House?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun (originally aired May 10, 2012) on the shotgun house, a long narrow single-file house style. The hosts cover its features (narrow lot, rooms in a straight line with aligned doors, high ceilings, later-added plumbing, front porches), its likely origins in West Africa (to gun / shogun in Yoruba), its spread to Haiti and then New Orleans after the Haitian Revolution, property tax quirks based on frontage and room count, the 1893 Atlanta Journal-Constitution classified ad, spread to Oklahoma and Atlanta neighborhoods, the front porch's role in community life, the 1906 San Francisco earthquake and cheap kit housing, pop culture references (David Byrne, John Mellencamp's "Pink Houses," Elvis Presley, Aaron Neville), and the tiny house movement. The episode closes with listener mail about a fan's encounter with the Beastie Boys in Las Vegas and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and David Byrne reference
segments.summary: Josh introduces the rerun and the topic of shotgun houses, mentions David Byrne's lyric about shotgun houses, and sets up the discussion of Hurricane Katrina and concern over losing the architecture.

segments.title: Defining features of the shotgun house
segments.summary: The hosts describe the long, narrow layout with rooms in a straight line and aligned doors, the narrow lots between houses, high ceilings, later-added plumbing, and the origin of the name from the shooting-through-the-doors story, which they say is probably not true.

segments.title: West African roots and the name from Yoruba
segments.summary: Chuck explains the decorative bracket carvings and that the design has older versions in Haiti and West Africa, where Yoruba words to gun or shogun are said to be the likely source of the name.

segments.title: New Orleans property taxes and the 1893 classified ad
segments.summary: The hosts discuss New Orleans taxes based on frontage and then room count, which shotgun houses avoided, the camelback variant, and the first known printed use of the term in a 1893 Atlanta Journal-Constitution classified ad.

segments.title: Haitian Revolution and spread from Haiti to New Orleans
segments.summary: The hosts trace how the Haitian Revolution led by Toussaint Louverture freed slaves and drove out white plantation owners, and how Haitian migrants brought the house style to New Orleans, a multiethnic city of that era.

segments.title: Spread across the US and related house types
segments.summary: The shotgun house spread to working-class African American neighborhoods in cities like Chicago and Atlanta, then to Oklahoma, including all-Black towns and areas with Native American tribes. The hosts also distinguish row houses and railroad houses.

segments.title: Front porches, cultural legacy, and history of research
segments.summary: Chuck explains that the front porch was a central part of community life, and that shotgun houses influenced later porch and stoop designs. The hosts also say the history was traced by historians only in recent decades, and they discuss the 1906 San Francisco earthquake, cheap kit housing, and disaster relief use.

segments.title: Pop culture, tiny houses, and closing recommendations
segments.summary: The hosts mention songs and famous people linked to shotgun houses, including John Mellencamp's Pink Houses, Elvis Presley, and Aaron Neville, and the modern tiny house movement. They suggest local landmarks and a visit to the King Memorial area in Atlanta.

segments.title: Listener mail: Beastie Boys encounter
segments.summary: A listener shares a story of meeting the Beastie Boys in Las Vegas as a teenager during the Licensed to Ill tour, followed by a request for listener stories about unusual homes or Beastie Boys encounters.
